https://rootandremedy-wellness.com/servi: What is IV therapy?

IV therapy delivers fluids, vitamins, minerals, and other nutrients straight into your bloodstream. Because the infusion bypasses your digestive system, your body absorbs the nutrients quickly and gets more of them than it would from oral supplements.
Which IV drip should I choose?

Start with your goal. The Hydration covers basic fluid and electrolyte needs, The Myers offers all-around immune and energy support, and The Root and Remedy lets your provider build a custom blend around your labs and health goals. Our team can help you choose when you arrive.
Where can I get IV therapy in Modesto or Turlock?
Root & Remedy Wellness offers IV therapy at 803 Coffee Rd Suite #2 in Modesto and 121 W Main Street Suite H in Turlock. You can book an appointment online or call 209-614-0605.
Can I add an injection to my IV?
Yes. Many of our injectable therapies work as add-ons to an infusion, including Zofran for nausea and Toradol for aches and inflammation when your provider approves them.
Do you offer IV therapy memberships?
Yes. If you plan to come in regularly, visit our IV Memberships page to see the current options.
What is in The Hydration IV?
The Hydration IV contains sterile saline solution that replenishes fluids and electrolytes. It focuses entirely on restoring hydration and balance at the cellular level.
Is IV hydration better than drinking water?

IV hydration works faster because fluids enter your bloodstream directly instead of passing through your digestive system. Oral hydration can take hours to absorb, while an IV delivers fluids and electrolytes to your cells right away.
Who should get The Hydration IV?
The Hydration suits anyone who feels dehydrated, drained, or foggy after illness, travel, or a demanding workout. It also makes a simple first infusion if you are new to IV therapy.
Can I add vitamins to The Hydration IV?
You can pair it with an injection such as Vitamin B12, or step up to The Myers if you want vitamins and minerals in the drip itself.
Can I combine any infusion with salt therapy?
Yes. You can relax in our Salt Room during your infusion, and we especially recommend the pairing when you are fighting an upper respiratory infection or looking for ultimate relaxation.
What is a Myers Cocktail?
The Myers Cocktail is an IV infusion of Vitamin C, B-Complex, Magnesium, Zinc, and B12. People have called it the original IV infusion since the 1960s.
What is the Myers Cocktail good for?

Our Myers IV supports immune health, acute or chronic health issues, energy, metabolism, sleep, and mood. Clients choose it for prevention pre travel, for recovery, and for acute or chronic health needs such as ongoing fatigue and stress.
What is the difference between The Myers and The Super Myers?

The Super Myers includes everything in The Myers plus a dose of glutathione, the body's master antioxidant. That addition brings extra support for inflammation and your body's natural detox processes.
Can I add NAD to a Myers IV?
Yes. Your provider may pair NAD with The Myers for combined metabolic and immune support, then confirm the right dose for you.
Where can I get a Myers Cocktail in Modesto or Turlock?
Both Root & Remedy Wellness locations offer The Myers. Schedule an appointment online or call 209-614-0605.
What is in The Super Myers IV?

The Super Myers combines the nutrients in The Myers (Vitamin C, B-Complex, Magnesium, Zinc, and B12) with a dose of glutathione. You get broad nutrient support and added antioxidant protection in one infusion.
Who is The Super Myers best for?
The Super Myers fits people who want immune support, energy restoration, detox support, and whole-body balance at the same time. Your provider customizes treatment to your individual health goals.
Why add glutathione to a Myers Cocktail?

Glutathione neutralizes free radicals and supports liver detoxification. Adding it to The Myers extends the infusion's reach to inflammation and detox support, which you can read more about on our Glutathione IV page.
Should I choose The Super Myers or The Clean Up for detox?

Pick The Clean Up if detox and liver support are your main goals, since it pairs glutathione with Taurine and B-complex. The Super Myers makes more sense when you also want the immune and energy support of a full Myers blend.
Is The Super Myers good for prevention or recovery?
Yes. The Super Myers works for both, whether you want to stay ahead of illness or you are recovering from an acute or chronic health concern.
What does The Renew IV do?
The Renew IV nourishes hair, skin, and nails from the inside out. Its blend of Vitamin C, Biotin, and Lysine supports collagen production, connective tissue strength, and overall radiance.
What is in The Renew IV?

The Renew contains three nutrients: Vitamin C for antioxidant protection and collagen synthesis, Biotin (B7) for keratin production, and Lysine, an amino acid that aids collagen formation and tissue repair.
Is IV beauty therapy better than topical skin care?

Topical products work on the surface, while The Renew delivers nutrients to your bloodstream for faster, more complete absorption. Your cells get the building blocks they need to repair and strengthen from within.
Can The Renew support hair growth and strength?
Yes. Biotin drives keratin production, the protein that forms the structure of hair, skin, and nails, so The Renew supports stronger hair at the cellular level.
What pairs well with The Renew?
You can add our Glutathione IV for antioxidant support and skin brightening.
What is in The Relax IV?
The Relax IV contains Magnesium and Lysine, with optional Toradol when your provider finds it clinically appropriate.
Can an IV help with stress and muscle tension?
The Relax targets both. Magnesium calms nerve excitability and relaxes muscles, while Lysine aids tissue repair, helping your body recover from stress, overexertion, and chronic tension.
What does Toradol add to The Relax?
Toradol is an anti-inflammatory medication that reduces pain signals. Your provider may include it if you are dealing with aches, pain, or inflammation.
How is The Relax different from The Cure?

The Relax focuses on stress, circulation, and muscle tension. The Cure targets acute support and or recovery from hangovers, stomach bugs, migraines, and dehydration, with optional medication for nausea or pain.
What else pairs well with The Relax?
Our Salt Room and infrared sauna both promote relaxation and stress relief, so either one rounds out a full reset.
What is The Recharge IV?
The Recharge IV fuels energy, muscle recovery, and performance for active lifestyles. It combines Vitamin C, amino acids, Magnesium, and B12.
Is The Recharge IV good for athletes?
Yes. Amino acids fuel muscle repair, magnesium supports muscle contraction and energy metabolism, and B12 helps red blood cells deliver oxygen for better endurance.
Should I get The Recharge IV or the Recharge injection?

Choose the IV when you want a full infusion with Vitamin C and magnesium. The Recharge IM injection delivers B vitamins and amino acids in a quick shot, which works well between infusions or on a busy day.
When should I book The Recharge IV?
Book it after heavy training, a competition, or any stretch of high physical demand when your body needs to refuel and repair.
Can I pair The Recharge with the infrared sauna?
Yes. Sauna sessions boost circulation and cause you to sweat out fluids and nutrients, and our infrared sauna page explains how to sequence it with an IV.
What is in The Clean Up IV?
The Clean Up combines Glutathione, Taurine, and B-complex vitamins to support detoxification, liver health, and reduced inflammation.
How does a detox IV support the liver?

The Clean Up supports your liver's natural detox pathways. Glutathione neutralizes free radicals, Taurine aids bile production and antioxidant defense, and B-complex powers the enzymes that drive detoxification.
Why get glutathione by IV instead of a pill or over the counter supplement?
IV delivery makes antioxidants like glutathione more bioavailable and active than oral forms, which your digestive system largely breaks down.
How does The Clean Up compare to the Glutathione IV?
The Glutathione IV delivers glutathione on its own for antioxidant and skin support. The Clean Up adds Taurine and B-complex for broader detox and liver support.
Can I pair The Clean Up with sauna therapy?
Yes. Our infrared sauna offers a dedicated Detox program, and pairing it with The Clean Up makes a strong detox-focused wellness day.
What is The Clarity IV?
The Clarity IV blends B-complex, B12, Magnesium, and Alpha Lipoic Acid to support brain and nerve health, focus, and balanced energy.
Can an IV help with brain fog?
The Clarity targets mental clarity and focus. B vitamins fuel energy metabolism and neurotransmitter production, while alpha lipoic acid protects neurons and improves mitochondrial efficiency.
Will The Clarity make me feel jittery?
No. Magnesium calms the nervous system, so The Clarity supports balanced energy without overstimulation.
What is alpha lipoic acid?
Alpha lipoic acid is a powerful antioxidant that protects nerve cells and supports long-term brain health. You can also get it as a standalone Alpha-Lipoic Acid IV.
How does The Clarity compare to NAD therapy?

Both support focus and mental clarity. The Clarity delivers a nutrient blend in a standard infusion time of 45-60 minutes, while NAD therapy restores a coenzyme tied to cellular energy and runs over 1.5 to 4 hours.
What is The Cure IV?
The Cure IV offers support and fast relief from stomach bugs, hangovers, migraines, and acute dehydration. It combines B-complex vitamins and Magnesium, with optional Zofran or Toradol.
Does an IV help with a hangover?
Yes. The Cure replenishes fluids and nutrients intravenously, so you recover faster than you would with oral remedies, and optional add-ons target nausea and headache pain.
What are Zofran and Toradol?

Zofran (ondansetron) is an anti-nausea medication, and Toradol (ketorolac) is an anti-inflammatory that reduces pain. Your provider decides whether to add either one based on your symptoms and health history.
Can The Cure help with headaches and migraines?
Yes. We designed The Cure to support headaches and migraines along with nausea and dehydration, and your provider may include Toradol for pain.
What if I only need nausea relief?

A stand alone Zofran IM injection gives you quick relief in a 5 to 10 minute appointment when you do not have time for a full infusion. If you have time for the infusion, you can elect to only add in Zofran.
What is in The Skinny IV?
The Skinny IV combines amino acids, Vitamin B12, and L-Carnitine to support metabolism, gut health, energy, and lean muscle recovery.
Does The Skinny IV help with weight loss?
The Skinny IV supports weight management by helping your body burn fuel more efficiently and by reducing cravings. It works best alongside healthy nutrition and regular movement.
What does L-Carnitine do?
L-Carnitine carries fatty acids into your mitochondria, where your cells convert them into usable energy. That process supports endurance and muscle recovery.
What is the difference between The Skinny IV and The Skinny injection?
The Skinny IV includes L-Carnitine and delivers its nutrients by infusion. The Skinny Injection delivers B12 and amino acids in a quick in-office shot, typically weekly or biweekly.
What is NAD IV therapy?

NAD IV therapy delivers nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), a coenzyme found in every living cell, directly into your bloodstream. NAD helps your cells produce energy, repair DNA, and support brain function.
How long does an NAD IV take?
An NAD infusion typically takes 1 to 4 hours, depending on your dose and tolerance. Our nurses monitor the infusion rate, your vital signs, and your comfort throughout the session.
What does an NAD infusion feel like?

Some people notice flushing, chest or abdominal tightness, headache, or nausea, especially when the infusion runs fast. A slower rate improves tolerance, and your provider can add Zofran or Toradol for comfort.
Do you offer NAD injections?

Yes. We offer NAD as an intramuscular or subcutaneous injection in smaller maintenance doses of 25 to 100 mg, usually weekly or biweekly. See options on our Injectable Therapy page or call 209-614-0605 for specific questions.
How often should I get NAD therapy?

Infusion protocols usually start with a loading series of weekly or biweekly infusions, followed by maintenance every 4 to 6 weeks. Paying attention to how you feel helps you decide when you are ready for the next one.
Who should use caution with NAD therapy?
Talk with your provider first if you have heart disease, liver or kidney impairment, or are pregnant or breastfeeding, since research in these groups is limited.
What is a glutathione IV?
A glutathione IV delivers the body's master antioxidant directly into your bloodstream. It protects cells from oxidative stress, supports liver detoxification, and promotes healthy, radiant skin.
Does glutathione help brighten skin?
Yes. Skin brightening and anti-aging support are among the benefits the Glutathione IV offers, along with detox, immune support, and reduced inflammation.
Why not just take glutathione pills?
Your digestive system absorbs oral glutathione poorly and breaks it down quickly. IV delivery bypasses that process and gets more glutathione to your cells.
Can I get a glutathione IV after a sauna session?
Yes. We recommend a Glutathione IV in additional fluid after time in our infrared sauna for antioxidant and hydration recovery.
Which other IVs include glutathione?
You will also find glutathione in The Super Myers, The Clean Up, and our seasonal Allergy Cure IV.
What is an alpha-lipoic acid IV?
The Alpha-Lipoic Acid (ALA) IV is an antioxidant infusion that supports cellular energy production, nerve health, inflammation, and detoxification.
What makes alpha-lipoic acid different from other antioxidants?
ALA works in both water- and fat-soluble environments, so it protects every part of the cell. It also regenerates other antioxidants, including Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and glutathione.
Can an ALA IV support nerve health?
Yes. ALA reduces oxidative stress in nerve cells and enhances glucose metabolism, which supports nerve health and helps calm inflammation.
Is IV alpha-lipoic acid better than oral ALA?
Your digestive system partially breaks down oral ALA. An IV delivers higher concentrations directly into your bloodstream for faster, more potent results.
Which other IV contains alpha-lipoic acid?
The Clarity includes ALA along with B-complex, B12, and magnesium to support focus and brain health.
What is The Root and Remedy IV?
The Root and Remedy is our signature custom infusion. Your provider designs it around your health assessment, lab results, and treatment goals after a focused or comprehensive evaluation.
What goes into a custom IV?
Your provider selects from targeted vitamins, minerals, amino acids, and antioxidants to meet your needs, whether you want more energy, stronger immunity, better recovery, or long-term balance.
Do I need lab work for a custom IV?

Your provider builds the blend from your health assessment and lab results, so recent labs help. For deeper testing, our Functional Medicine Packages include advanced diagnostics and in-depth consultations. Call 209-614-0605 for additional consultation options.
How is a custom IV different from a standard drip?
Standard drips like The Myers follow a set formula for common goals. The Root and Remedy changes with you, because your provider adjusts it to your labs and goals.
How do I book The Root and Remedy IV?
Schedule an appointment at our Modesto or Turlock location, or call 209-614-0605.
What is Venofer?
Venofer is iron sucrose, a stable, well-tolerated form of IV iron. It replenishes your iron stores directly through the bloodstream.
Who needs an iron infusion?

Iron IV therapy may help if you have iron deficiency anemia, heavy menstrual bleeding, pregnancy or postpartum iron needs, blood loss from surgery, a malabsorption condition, or iron depletion from intense training.
Is IV iron better than iron pills?
For many people, yes. Oral iron often upsets the stomach and absorbs poorly, while IV iron bypasses the gut and goes straight to your body's cells.
Do I need a prescription or labs for IV iron?

Yes. A physician prescribes Iron IV therapy, and your dose depends on your lab values, hemoglobin levels, and degree of deficiency. The prescription can come from your physician or through our physician.
What else supports low energy from anemia?
Vitamin B12 therapy supports healthy red blood cell production and can help when B12 deficiency plays a role. A Myers cocktail is a good option for well rounded support as well.
What is high-dose vitamin C IV therapy?
High-dose vitamin C IV therapy is a physician-ordered infusion that delivers potent antioxidant support. Your provider tailors the dose to your lab values and health and wellness goals.
Why get vitamin C through an IV?
Your gut limits how much vitamin C it can absorb. An IV bypasses digestion and delivers much higher concentrations straight into your bloodstream.
Who is high-dose vitamin C IV therapy for?

People consider it for immune support, chronic inflammation, recovery from surgery or injury, chronic fatigue, Lyme disease and chronic infections, detox support, and physician-directed adjunctive support during cancer treatment.
Is high-dose vitamin C safe?
A physician directs every high-dose vitamin C infusion, and lab monitoring guides your dose to maximize benefit and minimize risk.
How is this different from the vitamin C in The Myers?

The Myers includes vitamin C as part of a broad everyday blend. High-dose vitamin C therapy delivers a much larger dose, for targeted antioxidant and immune support. Vitamin C acts as a pro-oxidant that generates hydrogen peroxide in tissues. Laboratory and animal studies show this can selectively target and damage certain unwanted cells while sparing normal cells. Supportively, It also functions as an immune modulator, an enzyme cofactor, and an agent that can help lower inflammation.
What is The Allergy Cure IV?
The Allergy Cure is a seasonal infusion that supports your body during pollen and environmental allergy exposure. It blends Vitamin C, Vitamin B12, Magnesium, and Glutathione.
Can an IV help with seasonal allergies and sinuses?

The Allergy Cure supports immune balance and helps calm your inflammatory response to pollen, dust, and other airborne triggers. Vitamin C helps stabilize immune cells and supports your response to histamine.
When should I get the allergy IV?
Many clients book it during spring and fall, when pollen and airborne allergens peak.
Why does the allergy IV include glutathione?
Glutathione supports detox pathways and reduces the oxidative stress that environmental allergens cause.
What else helps with seasonal allergies and sinuses?
Our Salt Room offers drug-free support for allergies and congestion, and you can relax there during your infusion.
What are injectable therapies?

Injectable therapies deliver concentrated vitamins, minerals, and specialty compounds directly into the muscle. They give you a fast, convenient way to boost energy, support immunity, and aid recovery.
Which injections do you offer?
We offer Vitamin B12, Vitamin D, Recharge, NAD, and The Skinny for wellness support, plus Zofran for nausea and Toradol for inflammatory pain.
Should I get an injection or an IV?
Choose an injection when you want targeted support in a short visit. Choose IV therapy when you have more time and want hydration along with a broader blend of nutrients at 100% absorption.
Can I add an injection to my IV session?
Yes. You can add many of our injectables to an infusion to amplify its benefits.
How long does an injection appointment take?
Injection visits run much shorter than infusions. An injection, for example, fits into a 5 to 10 minute appointment.
What does a B12 shot do?
A B12 shot supports energy metabolism, red blood cell formation, and nervous system function. It quickly restores your levels when you run low.
Should I get B12 by IV or injection?

Choose IV when your goals are to support vitamin b12 deficiency at 100% absorption, rapid delivery and an energy boost. Choose an intramuscular injection for 'on the go' supplementation. Both options are supportive if you have absorption issues.
Who benefits from B12 injections?

B12 injections help people with fatigue, brain fog, B12 deficiency or pernicious anemia, tingling or numbness, malabsorption from conditions like Crohn's or celiac disease, and vegetarian or vegan diets.
Does a B12 injection have side effects?
Most people tolerate B12 well. You may notice mild redness or soreness at the injection site or temporary tingling, brief flushing, or a temporary jittery feeling.
Which IVs include B12?
The Myers, The Clarity, The Recharge, The Skinny IV, and The Allergy Cure all include B12.
What is a vitamin D injection?
A vitamin D injection replenishes this fat-soluble vitamin directly through the muscle. Vitamin D supports bone strength, immune function, cellular regulation, and mood.
What are the signs of vitamin D deficiency?
Common signs include fatigue, weakened immunity, bone or joint pain, and low mood. Limited sun exposure, diet, malabsorption, and certain health conditions can all cause a deficiency.
How often do I need a vitamin D injection?
Your provider typically schedules injections monthly, quarterly, or as prescribed, based on your lab values and how deficient you are.
Do I need lab work before a vitamin D injection?
Yes. We recommend testing before and during therapy to confirm optimal levels and prevent toxicity.
How do I get lab work to get a vitamin D injection?
You can bring in your recent results from your PCP or you can schedule a focused consultation with our provider who can order, if indicated.
Are vitamin D injections safe?

Most people tolerate them well, with occasional mild soreness or redness at the injection site. High doses require monitoring to avoid toxicity, high calcium, or kidney complications, so your provider bases your dose on your labs.
What is in the Recharge injection?
The Recharge IM injection combines B complex vitamins with an amino acid blend to support energy metabolism, muscle health and recovery, and performance.
Who should get the Recharge injection?
It suits anyone dealing with fatigue, high physical demands, or an active lifestyle that calls for extra energy and recovery support.
How often can I get the Recharge injection?
Most people receive it 1 to 2 times per month, though your provider may adjust the schedule to your goals.
What is the difference between the Recharge injection and The Recharge IV?
The injection delivers B vitamins and amino acids in a quick shot. The Recharge IV is a full infusion that adds Vitamin C and Magnesium as well as the hydration component.
What pairs well with the Recharge injection?
Pair it with The Hydration for enhanced recovery with 100% absorption of those nutrients, or add a session in our Salt Room to support full body energy and recovery.
What is The Skinny Injection?
The Skinny Injection combines Vitamin B12 and targeted amino acids to support metabolism, energy production, and lean muscle health.
Does The Skinny Injection help with weight loss?
It complements weight management goals by supporting metabolism, fat utilization, and appetite regulation. It delivers the best results alongside healthy nutrition and movement, not as a quick fix.
How often should I get The Skinny Injection?
Most clients receive it weekly or biweekly, depending on their goals.
Can I combine The Skinny Injection with an IV?
Yes. It pairs well with most infusions for added metabolic and energy support; however our registered nurses will monitor any double of nutrients.
Does The Skinny Injection have side effects?
Most people tolerate it well. Mild soreness at the injection site can occur, and a few people notice brief flushing or a temporary jittery feeling.
What is Zofran used for?
Zofran (ondansetron) is an anti-nausea medication that prevents and treats nausea and vomiting.
How does Zofran work?
Zofran blocks serotonin receptors in the gut and central nervous system that trigger nausea, so fewer nausea signals reach your brain.
Can I get Zofran as a shot or add it to an IV?
Both. You can add Zofran to any infusion, often The Hydration or The Cure, or get a standalone intramuscular injection in a quick 5 to 10 minute appointment.
Can Zofran be added to an NAD infusion?
Yes. Your provider can add Zofran to an NAD infusion to minimize nausea during treatment.
Does Zofran have side effects?
Zofran is generally well tolerated but may cause mild headache, constipation, or dizziness. Your provider uses caution if you have a heart rhythm disorder or certain liver conditions.
What is Toradol?
Toradol (ketorolac) is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that provides rapid relief from acute pain, inflammation, and muscle discomfort.
How does Toradol work?
Toradol blocks the COX enzymes that produce prostaglandins, the chemical messengers behind pain and swelling. Lower prostaglandin levels mean fewer pain signals and less inflammation.
Which IVs can include Toradol?
Your provider can add Toradol to The Relax, The Cure, and NAD infusions, or you can get it as a standalone add on or a 5-10 minute intramuscular injection.
How long can I use Toradol?
Providers use Toradol for short-term pain relief of up to 5 days because of potential kidney and gastrointestinal side effects.
Who should not get Toradol?
Toradol is not recommended if you have active gastrointestinal bleeding, severe kidney disease, or certain cardiovascular conditions. Your provider reviews your history and medications first.
What is halotherapy?
Halotherapy, or salt therapy, disperses dry micronized salt particles into a room with a halogenerator. You breathe the particles in, and they reach deep into your lungs and respiratory system.
What are the benefits of salt therapy?

Salt therapy helps clear mucus and congestion, may ease breathing for people with allergies, asthma, bronchitis, and sinusitis, and supports skin conditions like eczema and psoriasis. It also promotes deep relaxation.
How much does salt therapy cost?
A 30-minute session costs $30 and a 45-minute session costs $40. Family sessions cost $60, and you can add salt therapy to an IV for $30.
How long is a salt therapy session and how often should I go?
Sessions typically last 30 to 45 minutes, and you can come as often as you like.
What should I wear to the Salt Room?
Wear whatever you like. Salt may collect on your clothes, but it brushes off easily.
Can I do salt therapy during my IV?
Yes. You can relax in the Salt Room during your infusion, and the pairing works especially well with The Myers or The Hydration ESPECIALLY when you are fighting an upper respiratory infection.
What kind of sauna do you use?
We use the mPulse Conquer Sauna, which combines full-spectrum infrared (far, mid, and near) with red light therapy to reach deep into your tissues.
What sauna programs can I choose?
The mPulse Conquer offers six preset programs: Detox, Cardio, Relaxation, Pain Relief, Weight Loss, and Anti-Aging. You can also customize a session to your goals.
How long and how often should I use the infrared sauna?
Sessions typically last 20 to 45 minutes, and we recommend 1 to 3 sessions per week depending on your goals.
Should I get an IV before or after the sauna?

Get your IV first, then use the sauna to support detox and circulation, then rehydrate with electrolytes. If relaxation is your goal, you can reverse the order, and a Glutathione IV after the sauna adds antioxidant recovery.
Who should avoid infrared sauna therapy?

Use caution or check with your physician if you are pregnant, have uncontrolled hypertension or heart disease, severe anemia, a fever or acute infection, a recent stroke or seizure, or an implanted medical device. Avoid the sauna if you are under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
